paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.

model_annotations.German: The bar chart titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B Generation Length Comparison" visually compares the generation length (in words) of two reasoning methods—Vanilla CoT (light pink bars) and TLDR (Ours, dark red bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis represents generation length, scaled linearly from 0 to 8000 words with tick marks at intervals of 1000. The horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order. For each dataset, two bars are shown side-by-side, with the legend indicating that light pink corresponds to Vanilla CoT and dark red to TLDR (Ours). The chart demonstrates that TLDR consistently reduces generation length compared to Vanilla CoT: on GSM8K, generation length drops from 554 to 254 words (a -54% reduction); on MATH500, from 2861 to 1542 words (-46%); on AIME, from 6820 to 6330 words (-7%); and on AMC, from 4510 to 3380 words (-25%). Percent reductions are explicitly labeled above each dark red bar. The bars are not sorted by length but are grouped by dataset, and no visual emphasis (e.g., shading or annotations) is applied beyond the percentage labels. The data illustrates that TLDR significantly shortens output length across all datasets while maintaining or improving accuracy, as noted in the paper’s caption.
